text:
alex.s: :rotating_light: seeing sustained KV cache growth on prod-gpu pool since ~15:04 UTC. continuous-batching rate spiked and streaming responses started to stall (tokens arriving in bursts).

ops-bot: Alert: KV_CACHE_HIGH_GROWTH triggered on cluster prod-gpu-1 (90% increase in 10m).

maria.p: I can see per-pool metrics — kv_total_keys up 3x, prefix cache hit ratio dropping, per-request token latency jumping from 30ms -> 350ms for some routes.

jen.k: tagging @sre oncall. This looks like the same bloom-amplification pattern we've seen but with streaming cadence impact.

sre-oncall-bot: @sre-oncall is now on call: tao. Acknowledge to claim.

tao: ack. joining. quick ask: which model family/routes are affected?

alex.s: mostly chat routes hitting model-redwood/large-qat and some older fp16 variants. traffic skewed to long-context requests (≥8k) from a handful of customers.

kat: adding logs snippet showing KV cache eviction rate and batch sizes: ```
[2026-03-15T15:03:21Z] kv_evictions/s: 20 -> 120
[2026-03-15T15:04:10Z] continuous_batch_size: 4 -> 48
[2026-03-15T15:04:43Z] streaming_token_gap_ms: 10 -> 240
```

maria.p: hypothesis: a mis-tuned batching threshold plus a latent prefix growth led to continuous batching amplifying memory pressure, causing the runtime to pause token emission while reclaiming KV pages.

tao: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching on affected pool, 2) reduce batch max_tokens and raise eviction aggressiveness, 3) roll a canary config change to 10% of nodes.

jen.k: agree. prepare hotfix config. I'm pushing a canary that sets `continuous_batching.enabled=false` and `kv.eviction.target_ratio=0.6` for canary nodes.

ops-bot: Deploy started: config-canary/kv-throttle-1767890123 -> prod-gpu-1 (10% nodes).

alex.s: rolling canary now. monitoring logs for streaming token cadence.

(3m later)

kat: canary nodes show batch_size back to 6-8 and streaming token_gap down to ~20ms. customer-facing qps stable on canary.

maria.p: great. prepare to scale to 50% if no regressions. need a quick customer impact note for support.

tao: brief: impact window ~15:02-15:18 UTC. some long-context chat responses had delayed tokens; about ~0.4% of requests across the account surface saw >200ms per-token gaps, a handful of enterprise customers reported slow streaming. No dropped responses. Severity: P2 for now, escalating if rollback needed.

jen.k: increasing canary to 50%. ops-bot starting rollout.

ops-bot: Deploy update: config-canary -> 50% nodes.

alex.s: while we roll, I'm running a one-off eviction sweep to reclaim the largest stale prefixes on the remaining nodes: `./tools/kv-sweep --pool prod-gpu-1 --age 30m --limit 1000`

tao: note: sweep might cause brief CPU spikes. schedule during rollout and watch host load.

(10m later)

kat: sweep completed on canary hosts, no anomalies. streaming latency across canary and rolled hosts back to baseline.

maria.p: customer note draft: "We observed elevated token emission latency affecting streaming responses for a small subset of long-context requests between 15:02–15:18 UTC. We deployed a canary configuration disabling continuous batching for affected nodes and performed targeted eviction sweeps. Most customers returned to normal quickly; support will follow up individually with impacted customers." Thoughts?

jen.k: good. send to support and CSM. add troubleshooting link to grafana dashboard and the eviction command.

tao: post-mortem action items: - Add a guardrail to prevent continuous_batching.max_batch from exceeding 32 for long-context models. - Auto-detect prefix growth >2x in 5m and trigger soft-throttle. - Add an SLO alert for streaming_token_gap > 100ms on production.

alex.s: also add a runbook step to revert to a low-latency batching profile: `redwoodctl set profile low-latency --pool prod-gpu-1`

ops-bot: Deploy complete: config-canary -> 100% nodes.

kat: rolling metrics look stable for 9m post complete. no new alerts.

tao: I'm handing off to oncall-next (jen.k) for monitoring window. If anything spikes, escalate to infra.

sre-oncall-bot: Hand-off: tao -> jen.k (monitoring window 60m).

jen.k: ack. watching dashboards. will coordinate post-mortem.

maria.p: filing incident ticket (INC-2026-0315-kv-growth) with timeline, config diffs, and list of affected customer IDs (redacted). assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

alex.s: quick note for the postmortem: include an experiment log for any recent model variants we onboarded (qat changes) — they changed cache key sizes. Could be contributing.

tao: thanks all. great fast coordination. :white_check_mark:

(After handoff)

jen.k: minor follow-up: schedule a small canary of an eviction tuning blob for next week and add the guardrail as a pre-deploy check.

maria.p: marking incident resolved for now, severity downgraded to P3 after customer impact review.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-kv-growth marked RESOLVED by maria.p at 16:18 UTC.
